analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR DEFENSIVE POSTURING
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -22bps at 7,801 with a $4B market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX -21bps at 31,160, R2K -131bps at 2,793, Dow -66bps at 51,179. Volume was 16.4b shares vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.8b.
Defensive posturing under the surface (NDX > SPX > RTY) as global yields kept backing up. The GS US Cyclicals vs Defensives pair (GSPUCYDE) fell 159bps.

Russell underperformed NDX for the 4th straight day and 17 of the last 20 sessions. Small caps are absorbing the rates pressure. Some afternoon relief came from a 39bn 10-year auction that priced 1.6bps through at 5.3% (vs 5.316% when-issued).
GS floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, finishing -630bps for sale, driven mainly by macro products and to a smaller extent tech.

GS prime book net exposure to Mag7 is near 22% of total US exposure, the highest on record since the start of 2022, while overall market net positioning is still low. Semis and Semi Equipment are about 12% of total US exposure (June peak 14%, about 6% at the start of the year).
US Tech was the only sector net bought on the GS prime book in September, with its largest monthly buying since Feb 2025.
Costco August total comps were +11.4%, core comps +7.6%, US comp ex gas and FX +8%. The desk read the +8% as solid but at the low end of the +8-9% expectations it had heard.

Equity derivatives: vols were offered across the curve, most notably in NDX, and skew was bid. Flows were quiet apart from a couple of large hedging flows. Some activity in HYG and IYR. The desk sees gamma as cheap because today's implied move was realized intraday to the downside.
Buyers of 1-3 month upside in XLF, which is down 6% over the past month.

Financials earnings start next Tuesday with JPM, C and WFC reporting in the morning. September was a rough month for the sector, closing lower on 16 of 21 sessions, tied for the worst month since November 1999. The fourth quarter has historically been favorable for the sector.

market_movers.rationale: August total comps +11.4%, core +7.6%, US ex gas and FX +8%. Feedback was that the data was strong, but the +8% is at the low end of the +8-9% expected.

sector_views.rationale: September was among the worst months since 1999 (16 of 21 sessions down), but Q4 has historically been favorable. Earnings start next Tuesday.
Mag7 exposure on the GS prime book is the highest since early 2022 and tech was the only sector net bought in September, while semis exposure is below its June peak.

earnings_insights: Costco August sales update (reported after the close 10/7): total comps +11.4%, core comps +7.6%, US comp ex gas and FX +8%. The desk had heard expectations of +8-9% for the US ex gas and FX figure.
JPM, C and WFC report Q3 earnings next Tuesday morning (10/13), starting financials earnings season.
